Latin word

cujus

genitive of quis; plural quōrum, quārum

whose? of whom?; whose? (agreeing with the thing owned)

In this lexicon

  • whose

    the recommended word · classical · Plaut. Truc. 604–605: unde es? cujus es?

  • whose

    also used · classical · Verg. E. 3.1: cujum pecus?; Ter. And. 932: Cujam igitur?

  • cujus modī (cujusmodī): what kind of

    classical

Examples

  • dīc mihi, Dāmoetā, cujum pecus?

    tell me, Damoetas, whose flock is this?Verg. E. 3.1

    speak up: where are you from? whose are you?Plaut. Truc. 604–605

    don’t you know at whose house it is today?Petr. 26.4
